security_spec.violation_condition: In arch/riscv/kernel/entry.S and arch/riscv/mm/fault.c, the kernel reads CSR_TVAL into pt_regs->badaddr on every exception entry and uses it directly in handle_page_fault() for VMA lookup and signal delivery. If pointer masking (Zpm/Ssnpm) is enabled for a privilege mode, the hardware writes the *transformed* (masked) data-access address to stval for load/store page faults, but writes the *raw untransformed* instruction address for instruction page faults. The kernel violates the spec if it applies any additional pointer-unmasking or sign-extension transformation to stval values without first checking regs->cause to distinguish EXC_INST_PAGE_FAULT from EXC_LOAD_PAGE_FAULT/EXC_STORE_PAGE_FAULT, because the instruction-fault address is already the raw PC and would be corrupted by unmasking.
security_spec.summary: stval holds raw instruction addresses on EXC_INST_PAGE_FAULT but pointer-masked data addresses on EXC_LOAD/STORE_PAGE_FAULT; kernel page-fault code must not uniformly untag or transform stval without checking regs->cause
